title: The Missing Part
encoding: WebP quality94 from generated PNG, without resize or composition changes
sourceCredit: Devan Sandiford · The Moth, “The Re-Education of a Black Father”
imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: The Missing Part. Cast/design continuity: A fictional Black father with short close-cropped hair, warm dark-brown skin and muted blue shirt visiting a modest school classroom. Students are individually distinct children with varied skin tones and hairstyles; the questioning student wears an ochre sweater. Empty chalkboard, ordinary chairs. The father is not a likeness of the real source subject.. CELL 0: Wide classroom. Father sits at the front with hands poised in a practiced storytelling gesture; attentive children form a loose semicircle. A single faint incomplete blank speech-outline shape on the wall beside him has a conspicuous missing section, indicating an omission without any readable words. CELL 1: Same classroom. The child in ochre raises a hand then points gently toward the gap beside the father. Father stops mid-gesture and meets the child’s gaze. Leave real space between them; classmates stay quietly attentive rather than demanding or comforting. CELL 2: Father sits with hands lowered and open on his knees, looking directly at the children with a thoughtful, vulnerable expression. The faint incomplete blank speech-outline remains at the side, not covering faces. His posture accepts the hard part without asking the child to console him. CELL 3: Same father and classroom. He opens one hand in a careful, honest telling gesture; the once-incomplete pale speech-outline at the side becomes whole but remains entirely blank. Children listen with individual serious expressions. No historical reenactment, hateful imagery or vague kindness poster. CELL 4: The child in ochre speaks from their own chair, one hand lightly raised toward their own chest. Father turns fully to listen and keeps his hands still. A separate small blank outline sits near the child, clearly distinct from the father’s, with no text and no merged biography. CELL 5: Wide final classroom. Father and children share a quiet circle with open listening postures and separate faces; no one performs a grand inspirational reaction. The two small blank speech-outline motifs stay distinct at the edge, leaving room for individual accounts. No moral is written over the scene. Editorial limit: The dialogue explicitly names racism; do not replace that truth with a generic kindness lesson. No invented racist incident or hateful symbol; preserve separate child experience.
